stories.title: GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix
stories.summary: Netflix describes GenRec, an LLM-backed ranker that turns user histories and context into text, post-trains a foundation model for ranking, and scores the catalog in one pass. In the configuration reported, it beat a mature production baseline while using far fewer Phase-2 examples and input signals.
stories.why_it_matters: The paper is a rare production account of moving recommendation work from handcrafted feature interactions toward context design, reward integration, and constrained LLM serving, with online A/B evidence and explicit cost tradeoffs.
stories.action: Read it for the system design and evaluation method: separate foundation training from ranking adaptation, then inspect how context length, catalog constraints, reward signals, and serving cost shape the result.

sources.name: GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix — arXiv v2

body: Netflix reports GenRec as a two-phase LLM-backed recommendation ranker: foundation adaptation followed by ranking-specific post-training with recommendation data, labels, and reward signals.

The reported configuration verbalizes user history and context, constrains scoring to the catalog, and uses a cost-aware serving design. The paper presents offline results and a four-week online A/B test against a mature production ranker; its conclusions apply to the tested recommendation surfaces and configurations.
stories.author: Ying Li, Shradha Sehgal, Arjun Rao, Rein Houthooft, Yaochen Zhu, and Ashish Rastogi
